Where it began

Daryl Mitchell grew up around sport. His father, John, played rugby union and became a coach, and in 2006 the family moved to Western Australia when John was made head coach of the Western Force. Daryl spent five of his teenage years in Perth, playing his school cricket at Hale and his club cricket at Scarborough, and turning out for Western Australia's under-19 and under-23 sides.

In March 2009 he sat in the WACA dressing room celebrating a first-grade premiership with Scarborough team-mates who included Marcus Stoinis and Justin Langer. Good form in Perth's grade cricket brought him a contract with Northern Districts, and in 2012 he went back across the Tasman to join them, part-way through a degree in exercise and sports science.

The player

His Test debut came against England in November 2019, and his first Test hundred, an unbeaten 102 against Pakistan, in January 2021. Then came the summer of 2022. He was not expected to tour England at all, and was called in only to cover for an unavailable team-mate at Lord's. He made a hundred in each of the three Tests and 538 runs in the series at 107.60, more than any New Zealander had made in a Test series. He and Tom Blundell put on 611 runs together across the three matches.

By November 2026 he had played 39 Tests and made 2,411 runs at 43.05, with six hundreds, 16 fifties and a best of 190, and he had held 62 catches. In 2025 he became the top-ranked one-day batter in the world, the first New Zealander to get there since Glenn Turner in 1979.

What made him special

He was adaptable. At the 2021 T20 World Cup New Zealand needed an opener at short notice, and Mitchell, who had never opened in more than a hundred Twenty20 matches, did the job all tournament. His unbeaten 72 won the semi-final against England.

His bowling was more of an occasional pleasure. Four Test wickets at 102.50 each suggests his captains were right to keep him mostly in the field and the middle order.

Away from the middle

From 2018 to 2020, alongside his cricket, he helped keep the Waikato rugby players fit as an assistant conditioning coach. In that same 2021 semi-final he declined a run after realising he had got in the way of the bowler, Adil Rashid, and the ICC gave him its Spirit of Cricket award for it. Wisden also named him one of its Cricketers of the Year.

And finally

He became New Zealand's opener by accident and their record-breaking Test batter in England almost by accident too. With a rugby coach for a father and school rugby every winter, he could easily have ended up with an oval ball. Cricket was lucky the round one won.
